answer: Let reputation enter only through a narrow inlet: a newcomer must finish a public apprenticeship that strangers can watch, and its completed work stays on a horizon ledger open to inspection long after the task ends. A canyon rule then divides the map: influence earned in one community cannot cross into another without fresh local sponsors, so a copied identity arrives empty in each new place. Faking scale therefore means paying the apprenticeship price separately in every community, while a genuine newcomer pays once at home and carries its horizon record as portable proof of real effort.
